notes: Backend-declared, unmeasured by CERE. Lab only, not a twin of the production NVFP4 deployment: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next as ISTA-DASLab's GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS GGUF (3.0 bits per weight, 2 shards, sha256 equal to the release SHA256SUMS; owner's existing files), served by llama.cpp llama-server (commit 162e2bb2e, HIP gfx1151) behind cere-llamacpp-shim on AMD's Radeon 8060S. llama.cpp owns batching, KV cache and scheduling. MTP speculative decoding (llama.cpp draft-mtp, 3 draft tokens per round) from an MTP-only GGUF converted at bf16 by llama.cpp's own converter (convert_hf_to_gguf.py --mtp) from the official BF16 MTP tensors of Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next rev de4b8e4d plus its embed_tokens and lm_head; the artifact digest covers the two IQ3_XXS shards and that sidecar. Unlike the native CUDA path (spec output == plain), drafted greedy output is NOT bit-identical to plain greedy here: batched verification drifts at near-ties. KV cache f16, 4 slots sharing one 32768-token unified KV cache. Prefix caching is off for salted requests unless the shim runs with --trust-single-scope. Rows are concurrent CERE requests (1-4), not native batch rows. Structured output: response_format json_object/json_schema only, enforced by llama-server's own grammar (json_schema_to_grammar); keywords are those that pass CERE's enforcement variants on llama.cpp 162e2bb2e (bench/reports/amd-llamacpp-grammar-matrix-20261104.json) minus `format` (cered's format list is xgrammar's; llama.cpp enforces 4 of its 13 values). regex and ebnf are refused (the shim returns 400). Tool calls (tool_choice auto/none, unary and streamed): the tools are rendered by the model's template (passed as chat_template_kwargs.tools, byte-identical prompt) and the reply is parsed by CERE's qwen3_coder detector with SGLang d4689328e's value conversion (scripts/live/amd/qwen3_coder_convert.py, equal on all 4,574 tool_convert_cases), not by llama.cpp's stricter parser. Required/named tool_choice and parallel_tool_calls false are refused by the shim (400). Seeded sampling is unsupported. Not a throughput or capacity claim.
